Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) via 'name' Parameter — Unauthenticated remote code execution; attacker can read secrets, exfiltrate environment variables (including SUPER_SECRET_TOKEN), traverse the filesystem, or spawn reverse shells. [verified: The user-supplied `name` parameter is interpolated via f-string directly into the Jinja2 template source string (`content = f"

Hello, {name}!

..."`) before being passed to `Template(content).render()`, so Jinja2 expressions in `name` (e.g. `{{7*7}}`) are compiled and executed. The WAF rule that targets `{{.*}}` is entirely disabled (`SecRuleEngine Off`), and there is no other sanitization, ]

Hardcoded Credentials / Secret Token in Source Code — Anyone with read access to the repository (or a Docker image built from it) obtains the SUPER_SECRET_TOKEN and SUPER_SECRET_NAME, enabling credential replay or account takeover if the token is used elsewhere. [verified: Both SUPER_SECRET_TOKEN ('5u93R53Cr3tT0k3n') and SUPER_SECRET_NAME ('John Ripper') are hardcoded as Python literals in app/config.py lines 13 and 15 with FIXME comments acknowledging the issue; no env-var override is loaded because os.getenv() is commented out, so the secrets ship verbatim in source and any built Docker image. There is no secrets-management control in place — the docker-compose.ya]

Reflected XSS via 'name' Query Parameter — Attacker can execute arbitrary JavaScript in a victim's browser via a crafted link, enabling session hijacking, credential theft, or defacement. [verified: The `name` query parameter is embedded unescaped into raw HTML returned with `Content-Type: text/html` (via `HTMLResponse`/`Template.render()`), so a payload like `` is reflected verbatim to the browser. Missing Authentication on All Endpoints — Any unauthenticated attacker on the internet can invoke all application functionality, including the SSTI sink, without any credential. [verified: The `GET /` endpoint has no authentication decorator, middleware, API key check, or bearer token validation anywhere in `main.py` or the application stack; `SUPER_SECRET_TOKEN` is defined in `config.py` but never referenced in any auth check. Any unauthenticated internet user can reach the SSTI and XSS sinks directly.]

Missing Rate Limiting — DoS and Cost Amplification — Attacker can cause denial of service by exhausting server resources or incur financial cost by flooding requests that each trigger external HTTP calls. [verified: No rate-limiting middleware (slowapi, limits, or otherwise) is applied to the `GET /` endpoint, and the Caddy WAF is disabled (`SecRuleEngine Off`). Every request unconditionally triggers a synchronous `requests.get()` to an external service, meaning an attacker can flood the endpoint to exhaust outbound connections and amplify external HTTP costs without restriction.]

SUPER_SECRET_NAME Exposed as OpenAPI Schema Default Parameter Value — The hardcoded secret name is publicly disclosed via the auto-generated OpenAPI schema endpoint to any unauthenticated user, leaking a configuration secret intended to be private. [verified: SUPER_SECRET_NAME is hardcoded as 'John Ripper' in config.py and used as the default value for the `name` query parameter at main.py:19; FastAPI serializes parameter defaults into /openapi.json, exposing this value to any unauthenticated caller. While 'John Ripper' is a low-sensitivity name-like value rather than a cryptographic secret, it is a configuration secret intended to be private and its e]

Missing HTTP Security Headers — Absence of CSP and X-Frame-Options enables clickjacking and widens the XSS attack surface; missing X-Content-Type-Options allows MIME-sniffing attacks. [verified: Neither `main.py` nor the Caddyfile sets `Content-Security-Policy`, `X-Frame-Options`, `X-Content-Type-Options`, or `Strict-Transport-Security` headers; the WAF that could have added them is disabled. The absence of CSP meaningfully widens the already-confirmed XSS attack surface and enables clickjacking.]
